solution: Use \(\int \sqrt{a^2 - x^2}\,dx = \frac{x}{2}\sqrt{a^2 - x^2} + \frac{a^2}{2}\sin^{-1}\frac{x}{a} + C\) with \(a = 2\). So \(\int \sqrt{4 - x^2}\,dx = \frac{x}{2}\sqrt{4 - x^2} + 2\sin^{-1}\frac{x}{2} + C\).

Put \(u = 2x\), \(du = 2\,dx\): \(\int \sqrt{1 - 4x^2}\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\int \sqrt{1 - u^2}\,du = \frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{u}{2}\sqrt{1 - u^2} + \frac{1}{2}\sin^{-1}u\right] + C\). Back-substituting \(u = 2x\): \(= \frac{x}{2}\sqrt{1 - 4x^2} + \frac{1}{4}\sin^{-1}(2x) + C\).

Complete the square: \(x^2 + 4x + 6 = (x+2)^2 + 2\). With \(t = x+2\) and \(a^2 = 2\), \(\int \sqrt{t^2 + a^2}\,dt = \frac{t}{2}\sqrt{t^2 + a^2} + \frac{a^2}{2}\log\left|t + \sqrt{t^2 + a^2}\right| + C\). So \(\int \sqrt{x^2 + 4x + 6}\,dx = \frac{x+2}{2}\sqrt{x^2 + 4x + 6} + \log\left|x + 2 + \sqrt{x^2 + 4x + 6}\right| + C\).

Complete the square: \(x^2 + 4x + 1 = (x+2)^2 - 3\). With \(t = x+2\), \(a^2 = 3\), use \(\int \sqrt{t^2 - a^2}\,dt = \frac{t}{2}\sqrt{t^2 - a^2} - \frac{a^2}{2}\log\left|t + \sqrt{t^2 - a^2}\right| + C\). So \(\int \sqrt{x^2 + 4x + 1}\,dx = \frac{x+2}{2}\sqrt{x^2 + 4x + 1} - \frac{3}{2}\log\left|x + 2 + \sqrt{x^2 + 4x + 1}\right| + C\).

Complete the square: \(1 - 4x - x^2 = 5 - (x+2)^2\). With \(t = x+2\), \(a^2 = 5\), use \(\int \sqrt{a^2 - t^2}\,dt = \frac{t}{2}\sqrt{a^2 - t^2} + \frac{a^2}{2}\sin^{-1}\frac{t}{a} + C\). So \(\int \sqrt{1 - 4x - x^2}\,dx = \frac{x+2}{2}\sqrt{1 - 4x - x^2} + \frac{5}{2}\sin^{-1}\frac{x+2}{\sqrt{5}} + C\).

Complete the square: \(x^2 + 4x - 5 = (x+2)^2 - 9\). With \(t = x+2\), \(a^2 = 9\), use \(\int \sqrt{t^2 - a^2}\,dt = \frac{t}{2}\sqrt{t^2 - a^2} - \frac{a^2}{2}\log\left|t + \sqrt{t^2 - a^2}\right| + C\). So \(\int \sqrt{x^2 + 4x - 5}\,dx = \frac{x+2}{2}\sqrt{x^2 + 4x - 5} - \frac{9}{2}\log\left|x + 2 + \sqrt{x^2 + 4x - 5}\right| + C\).

Complete the square: \(1 + 3x - x^2 = \frac{13}{4} - \left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2\). With \(t = x - \frac{3}{2}\), \(a^2 = \frac{13}{4}\), use \(\int \sqrt{a^2 - t^2}\,dt = \frac{t}{2}\sqrt{a^2 - t^2} + \frac{a^2}{2}\sin^{-1}\frac{t}{a} + C\). So \(\int \sqrt{1 + 3x - x^2}\,dx = \frac{2x - 3}{4}\sqrt{1 + 3x - x^2} + \frac{13}{8}\sin^{-1}\frac{2x - 3}{\sqrt{13}} + C\).

Complete the square: \(x^2 + 3x = \left(x + \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 - \frac{9}{4}\). With \(t = x + \frac{3}{2}\), \(a^2 = \frac{9}{4}\), use \(\int \sqrt{t^2 - a^2}\,dt = \frac{t}{2}\sqrt{t^2 - a^2} - \frac{a^2}{2}\log\left|t + \sqrt{t^2 - a^2}\right| + C\). So \(\int \sqrt{x^2 + 3x}\,dx = \frac{2x + 3}{4}\sqrt{x^2 + 3x} - \frac{9}{8}\log\left|x + \frac{3}{2} + \sqrt{x^2 + 3x}\right| + C\).

Write \(\sqrt{1 + \frac{x^2}{9}} = \frac{1}{3}\sqrt{9 + x^2}\). With \(a = 3\), use \(\int \sqrt{x^2 + a^2}\,dx = \frac{x}{2}\sqrt{x^2 + a^2} + \frac{a^2}{2}\log\left|x + \sqrt{x^2 + a^2}\right| + C\): \(\frac{1}{3}\int \sqrt{x^2 + 9}\,dx = \frac{1}{3}\left[\frac{x}{2}\sqrt{x^2 + 9} + \frac{9}{2}\log\left|x + \sqrt{x^2 + 9}\right|\right] + C = \frac{x}{6}\sqrt{x^2 + 9} + \frac{3}{2}\log\left|x + \sqrt{x^2 + 9}\right| + C\).

Put \(t = x^2 + 1\), so \(dt = 2x\,dx\). Limits: \(x = 0 \Rightarrow t = 1\), \(x = 1 \Rightarrow t = 2\). Then \(\int_{0}^{1} \frac{x}{x^2 + 1}\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\int_{1}^{2} \frac{dt}{t} = \frac{1}{2}\left[\log t\right]_{1}^{2} = \frac{1}{2}\log 2\).

Write \(\cos^5\phi = (1 - \sin^2\phi)^2 \cos\phi\) and put \(t = \sin\phi\), \(dt = \cos\phi\,d\phi\). Limits: \(\phi = 0 \Rightarrow t = 0\), \(\phi = \frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow t = 1\). Then \(\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sqrt{\sin\phi}\,\cos^5\phi\,d\phi = \int_{0}^{1} t^{1/2}(1 - t^2)^2\,dt = \int_{0}^{1}\left(t^{1/2} - 2t^{5/2} + t^{9/2}\right)dt = \left[\frac{2}{3}t^{3/2} - \frac{4}{7}t^{7/2} + \frac{2}{11}t^{11/2}\right]_{0}^{1} = \frac{2}{3} - \frac{4}{7} + \frac{2}{11} = \frac{64}{231}\).

Put \(x = \tan\theta\); for \(x \in [0, 1]\), \(\theta \in [0, \frac{\pi}{4}]\), so \(\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{2x}{1 + x^2}\right) = \sin^{-1}(\sin 2\theta) = 2\theta = 2\tan^{-1}x\). Then \(\int_{0}^{1} \sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{2x}{1 + x^2}\right)dx = 2\int_{0}^{1} \tan^{-1}x\,dx = 2\left[x\tan^{-1}x - \frac{1}{2}\log(1 + x^2)\right]_{0}^{1} = 2\left(\frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{1}{2}\log 2\right) = \frac{\pi}{2} - \log 2\).

Put \(x + 2 = t^2\), so \(x = t^2 - 2\), \(dx = 2t\,dt\). Limits: \(x = 0 \Rightarrow t = \sqrt{2}\), \(x = 2 \Rightarrow t = 2\). Then \(\int_{0}^{2} x\sqrt{x + 2}\,dx = \int_{\sqrt{2}}^{2} (t^2 - 2)\,t\,(2t\,dt) = \int_{\sqrt{2}}^{2}\left(2t^4 - 4t^2\right)dt = \left[\frac{2}{5}t^5 - \frac{4}{3}t^3\right]_{\sqrt{2}}^{2} = \frac{32}{15} - \left(-\frac{16\sqrt{2}}{15}\right) = \frac{16(2 + \sqrt{2})}{15}\).

Put \(t = \cos x\), so \(dt = -\sin x\,dx\). Limits: \(x = 0 \Rightarrow t = 1\), \(x = \frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow t = 0\). Then \(\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \frac{\sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}\,dx = -\int_{1}^{0} \frac{dt}{1 + t^2} = \int_{0}^{1} \frac{dt}{1 + t^2} = \left[\tan^{-1}t\right]_{0}^{1} = \frac{\pi}{4}\).

Complete the square: \(x + 4 - x^2 = \frac{17}{4} - \left(x - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2\). With \(u = x - \frac{1}{2}\), \(a = \frac{\sqrt{17}}{2}\), use \(\int \frac{du}{a^2 - u^2} = \frac{1}{2a}\log\left|\frac{a + u}{a - u}\right|\). Then \(\int_{0}^{2} \frac{dx}{x + 4 - x^2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}\left[\log\left|\frac{\frac{\sqrt{17}}{2} + x - \frac{1}{2}}{\frac{\sqrt{17}}{2} - x + \frac{1}{2}}\right|\right]_{0}^{2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}\left[\log\frac{\sqrt{17} + 3}{\sqrt{17} - 3} - \log\frac{\sqrt{17} - 1}{\sqrt{17} + 1}\right] = \frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}\log\frac{5 + \sqrt{17}}{5 - \sqrt{17}}\).

Complete the square: \(x^2 + 2x + 5 = (x + 1)^2 + 4\). Then \(\int_{-1}^{1} \frac{dx}{(x + 1)^2 + 2^2} = \frac{1}{2}\left[\tan^{-1}\frac{x + 1}{2}\right]_{-1}^{1} = \frac{1}{2}\left(\tan^{-1}1 - \tan^{-1}0\right) = \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{8}\).

Notice \(\frac{d}{dx}\!\left(\frac{e^{2x}}{2x}\right) = \frac{2e^{2x}\cdot 2x - e^{2x}\cdot 2}{4x^2} = e^{2x}\left(\frac{1}{x} - \frac{1}{2x^2}\right)\), so the integrand is an exact derivative. Then \(\int_{1}^{2}\left(\frac{1}{x} - \frac{1}{2x^2}\right)e^{2x}\,dx = \left[\frac{e^{2x}}{2x}\right]_{1}^{2} = \frac{e^4}{4} - \frac{e^2}{2}\).

Divide the numerator and put \(u = \sin^2 x\), so \(du = 2\sin x\cos x\,dx\) and \(\cos^4 x + \sin^4 x = (1 - u)^2 + u^2 = 2u^2 - 2u + 1\). Limits: \(x = 0 \Rightarrow u = 0\), \(x = \frac{\pi}{4} \Rightarrow u = \frac{1}{2}\). Then \(\int_{0}^{\pi/4} \frac{\sin x\cos x}{\cos^4 x + \sin^4 x}\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{1/2} \frac{du}{2u^2 - 2u + 1} = \frac{1}{4}\int_{0}^{1/2} \frac{du}{\left(u - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{1}{4}} = \frac{1}{2}\left[\tan^{-1}(2u - 1)\right]_{0}^{1/2} = \frac{1}{2}\left(0 - \left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right) = \frac{\pi}{8}\).

Divide numerator and denominator by \(\cos^2 x\): the integrand becomes \(\frac{1}{1 + 4\tan^2 x}\). Put \(t = \tan x\), \(dx = \frac{dt}{1 + t^2}\); limits \(t: 0 \to \infty\). Then \(I = \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{dt}{(1 + 4t^2)(1 + t^2)}\). By partial fractions \(\frac{1}{(1 + t^2)(1 + 4t^2)} = \frac{-\frac{1}{3}}{1 + t^2} + \frac{\frac{4}{3}}{1 + 4t^2}\), so \(I = -\frac{1}{3}\cdot\frac{\pi}{2} + \frac{4}{3}\cdot\frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}(2t)\Big|_{0}^{\infty} = -\frac{\pi}{6} + \frac{4}{3}\cdot\frac{\pi}{4} = -\frac{\pi}{6} + \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\pi}{6}\).

Since \((\sin x - \cos x)^2 = 1 - \sin 2x\), put \(t = \sin x - \cos x\), so \(dt = (\cos x + \sin x)\,dx\) and \(\sqrt{\sin 2x} = \sqrt{1 - t^2}\). Limits: \(x = \frac{\pi}{6} \Rightarrow t = \frac{1 - \sqrt{3}}{2}\), \(x = \frac{\pi}{3} \Rightarrow t = \frac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{2}\). Then \(\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} \frac{\sin x + \cos x}{\sqrt{\sin 2x}}\,dx = \int_{(1-\sqrt{3})/2}^{(\sqrt{3}-1)/2} \frac{dt}{\sqrt{1 - t^2}} = \left[\sin^{-1}t\right]_{(1-\sqrt{3})/2}^{(\sqrt{3}-1)/2} = 2\sin^{-1}\frac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{2}\).

Since \(\sin 2x = 1 - (\sin x - \cos x)^2\), put \(t = \sin x - \cos x\), \(dt = (\cos x + \sin x)\,dx\), so \(9 + 16\sin 2x = 25 - 16t^2\). Limits: \(x = 0 \Rightarrow t = -1\), \(x = \frac{\pi}{4} \Rightarrow t = 0\). Then \(\int_{0}^{\pi/4} \frac{\sin x + \cos x}{9 + 16\sin 2x}\,dx = \int_{-1}^{0} \frac{dt}{25 - 16t^2} = \frac{1}{40}\left[\log\left|\frac{\frac{5}{4} + t}{\frac{5}{4} - t}\right|\right]_{-1}^{0} = \frac{1}{40}\left(0 - \log\frac{1}{9}\right) = \frac{1}{40}\log 9 = \frac{1}{20}\log 3\).

Put \(t = \sin x\), so \(dt = \cos x\,dx\) and \(\sin 2x\,dx = 2\sin x\cos x\,dx = 2t\,dt\). Limits: \(x = 0 \Rightarrow t = 0\), \(x = \frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow t = 1\). Then \(\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin 2x\,\tan^{-1}(\sin x)\,dx = 2\int_{0}^{1} t\tan^{-1}t\,dt = 2\left[\frac{t^2}{2}\tan^{-1}t - \frac{1}{2}(t - \tan^{-1}t)\right]_{0}^{1} = 2\left(\frac{\pi}{8} - \frac{1}{2} + \frac{\pi}{8}\right) = \frac{\pi}{2} - 1\).
